svg.text: Rocker J (CRF-style, pivots on the arm lug, curved arm up to the shock) — test print. Right side, front to the right
Arm at 20° full droop, XR250R shock 380 / 95. All sizes mm. Lug hole 12.8 (M12), other holes 10.8 (M10 + 0.8). 1:1 DXF and SVG next to this drawing.
Pivot on swingarm lug (M12)

curve bows 40 mm forward of the
straight line: passes through the arm
in front of the cross-member. Reshape to suit.
In place: full droop (solid) and full bump (outline)
swingarm pivot

XL lower mount

Link (rocker to XL lower mount)
101.8 centres
What it should do
• About 300 mm wheel travel with the XR shock, ratio 3.2 falling to 3.0 (7% rising rate)
• The rocker hardly turns on the arm (under 1°): it acts like a shock bracket on the arm
• Spring about 210-220 N/mm (twice G) and a revalve. Shock works ~40% harder
• Custom 380 / 120 shock on the same rocker: about 374 mm (too much: use a shorter stroke)
Check on the bike
• Does the curved arm pass through the swingarm in front of the cross-member?
• Clearance to the shock body and clevis around the shock eye
• Plate 16 mm (XR clevis gap); lug gap is about 41 mm, so pack it out
